keep: The idea is named up front: a battery is not a fixed tank, it gives fewer ampere-hours faster or colder, and Peukert's fit through two ratings estimates how many fewer.
One model carries the lesson: the battery as an emf behind a small r, so the terminals read E − Ir, and the same lost volts explain why a fast discharge reaches its end voltage sooner.

Worked numbers from the rule: 0.70 V lost and 11.90 V at 100 A; n = log 10 ÷ log 5.6 = 1.34 from the two ratings; 25 A gives about 2 hours 20 minutes and 58 Ah, against 4 hours from the fixed-tank sum and 67 Ah from the 1.25 default.

Each named slip has a DO screen with a hint per wrong pick: emf as terminal voltage (2), the battery as a constant-current source (4), the fixed tank (6), Peukert as exact (10), no emf with nothing connected (11).

Every number has a kind: the six cells, 7 mΩ, 25 A and the 14 mΩ cold figure are worded as examples or sketches; 2.1 V, 100 Ah, 20 h, 56 Ah, 1.00, 1.25 and the 27 °C and −18 °C figures are cited; the rest are computed.
Peukert is shown as a fit: the shaded region past 28 A, the hollow dot with 'real battery: less', and the closing sentence that a real battery gives even less at very high currents.
fix: Causal step skipped: why Peukert's rule is a straight line on log-log axes with gradient 1 − n. Add that capacity is current times time, so it goes as current to the power 1 − n, and a power law is straight on log-log axes with its power as the gradient.
Causal step skipped: why halving the load's resistance only nearly doubles the current. Give I = E ÷ (R + r): r stays in the sum.
Misconception not shown failing in numbers: 'Using 12.6 V there is the common slip' says it is a slip but not what it costs. Say it over-reads by the 0.70 V lost.
The brief's recall opener is missing: the gradient of a power law on log-log axes, with 'Still there' on the right pick. Add it as screen 1, making 13 screens, as lesson 1 has.

False absolute in the rule of thumb: 'the label's ampere-hours hold only at the label's rate' (temperature matters too, and slower gives more). Say the label's figure is for the label's rate and temperature.
Talks about the lesson: 'Both start from one picture of what a working battery is.' Cut it.
Units jump: r is given as 7 mΩ, then used as 0.007 without saying so. Give both once.
Long sentences: the log-log line sentence runs to 23 words, and '56 Ah, which is 28 A' reads awkwardly. Split both.
Ignores should say the cold scaling is the same fraction at every current, a simplification.

shape.ruleInWords: yes: terminal voltage is E − Ir; current to the power n times run time stays the same
shape.workedExampleWithRealNumbers: yes (100 A: 11.90 V; 25 A: 58 Ah, 2 hours 20 minutes)
shape.misconceptionShownFailing: partly: the fixed tank fails in numbers (4 hours against 2.3), the emf slip is named without its cost (fix)
shape.analogyWithBreak: yes: volt drop on a long final circuit; breaks on fixed cable resistance and on the acid reaching the plates
